scenes.title: Turner Geotechnical Centrifuge Chamber
scenes.institution: University of Cambridge — Schofield Centre Turner geotechnical centrifuge chamber
scenes.reference_notes: Historical facility photograph and original designer Philip Turner drawings inform the polygonal underground chamber, upper corridor, separate lower drive space, four hollow rectangular arm members, end bridges, parked swing-platform exteriors and a continuous shaft in two bearing housings. The stated 14 m shell diameter is interpreted as nominal inner diameter; the original datum remains unresolved. Four approximately 400 by 200 mm members follow the published section; wall thickness, elevations, bearing supports and local fit are estimated. The two original low-speed inspection controls operate an authored maintenance overlay; no OEM swing or high-g dynamics are implemented.
observed_cues: Official photograph shows the long centrifuge beam spanning a low concrete chamber. A central hub supports a broad rectangular equipment platform; each end has a bulky attachment beneath the beam. Foreground has a recessed metal floor grate; shallow overhead beams and fluorescent lights constrain vertical clearance.

scenes.title: EQUALS Structural Shaking-Table Bay
scenes.institution: University of Bristol — EQUALS earthquake shaking-table laboratory
scenes.reference_notes: Overhead photograph shows an experimental yellow braced frame bolted on a square shaking platform. Platform is recessed in a concrete pit with visible cylinders, hoses and metal edge railings. Surrounding floor has marked access lanes; separate actuator hardware stands at one edge. Photograph identifies the experimental bay, not the complete hall. Test frame is one historical specimen, not permanent lab equipment. No material failure or seismic response solver is implied.

scenes.title: Wind Tunnel A Model Test Bay
scenes.institution: Technical University of Munich — Aerodynamics and Fluid Mechanics Wind Tunnel A
scenes.reference_notes: Two official photographs show the enclosed test bay, including a supported model fixture and a vehicle model on the test floor. The large tunnel opening faces an instrumented platform with a circular floor insert; a safety chain borders the approach. A rail-supported overhead lifting beam and high wall panels are visible around the vehicle test station. A second official interior panorama shows amber test-floor panels, a circular inset and a framed traverse surrounding the tunnel opening; its wide-angle distortion is not a measured plan. Photographs establish the test bay; exterior duct photo was also checked and is not substituted for an interior. The small composite limits fine-detail recovery. Vehicle shown is a test specimen. Published cross-section dimensions anchor scale; enclosure dimensions, hidden ductwork and current configuration remain unverified. Airflow/aerodynamic results require a separate validated solver.

scenes.title: LITAC Laboratory Yarn-Spinning Workstation
scenes.institution: University of Leeds — LITAC laboratory-scale yarn spinning area
scenes.reference_notes: A working laboratory photograph shows a blue-and-white MESDANLAB fibre-to-yarn machine with a sloping side casing. Exposed rows of small rollers and guides lead to lower vertical yarn stations. A nearby touch panel is supported at standing operator height; white walls and a rear work surface are visible. Only the spinning-machine workstation is visually established. The page also covers knitting, extrusion and other separate laboratories; these must not be fused into one imagined room. No fibre formation, tension-control or textile constitutive solver is verified.
